content.content: When `deccy validate` finds failures, the deccy CLI shall write one line to stdout per failure as `<check> <id> <reason>`. When a check in that run could not itself run, the deccy CLI shall also write one line to stdout for it, alongside the failure lines and in the same three positions: the check's name, then a stand-in in the id position marking that no single node or change is implicated, and then the evidence that check produced. The line form is general to any check that could not itself run; a custody check that could not itself run, for example, is written `custody - <jj evidence>`.
content.rationale: Pipes and agents need per-failure handles naming the failed check, the node, and the reason; exit 2 on failures would collide with the O1/O2 refusal shape since a multi-line stdout report cannot be a refusal, and a reserved status 1 re-opens S4-one-free. Failures are reports rather than refusals, so O4 forces exit 0 always. One `<check> <id> <reason>` line keeps the report greppable under O5's line discipline. A check that never ran leaves no failure line, so a caller reading the report alone would see a clean run; giving that case a line of its own keeps the report answerable to every check the run attempted. The line reuses the three positions instead of a shape of its own, and its id position carries a stand-in because no single node or change is implicated there, so a reader still splits any line the same way. The stand-in glyph and the third position are fixed here so the form is one shape rather than a convention each check invents, while what the evidence holds stays with the checks. Which checks exist, what becomes of a case that cannot run, and the status it returns stay with the nodes that own them. States only the rendering fact without re-deciding D16c's exercising, D9's checks, O4's status rule, O5's channel rules, or sspsomkw's verdict-freedom.
